body:
[aida:advisor] IT IS NOT UNRECOVERABLE. I recovered it in full, and two of its four findings are ones nobody else raised - including one that is a live defect in this repo.

WHERE IT WAS. The headless reviewer session log:

    .aida/headless-logs/pr-2040-01a0c18e-f7eb-71e3-813b-f6fbaf1d4af4.jsonl

It captured the complete `aida review record` invocation - verdict, sha, branch, summary and all four --finding values verbatim. The overwritten verdict was the CODEX DRAIN REVIEWER's, run_uuid 01a0c17c, phase 3, recorded around 18:26. `.aida/events.jsonl` independently corroborates it: a PhaseEntered reviewer event and a SpecShelved with kind `verdict:request-changes`. So the FACT and KIND were in events.jsonl, and the CONTENT was in the session log. You checked the verdict directory, git, and the forge - three places it genuinely was not. Neither of us looked at the logs the drain writes for itself.

I have preserved it as a comment on BUG-1454, because a spec comment is git-backed and cannot be silently replaced, which the verdict file can.

THE TWO FINDINGS THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN LOST, and both are yours to weigh since they are now binding:

FINDING 4, promoted to BUG-1454 acceptance criterion 8, and the most consequential thing in this exchange. `specs_with_open_prs` returns an EMPTY MAP for every non-GitHub forge, and an empty map is read as "definitively no open PR", which permits completion. That directly violates criterion 3 of that very spec - prefer Done where the bump is ambiguous - and unqueried forge state is ambiguous, not negative. This project has a live GitLab mirror, so it is reachable here, not hypothetical.

FINDING 3, promoted to criterion 9. The regression fixture creates only ONE local commit and its fake gh returns PR #1979 for every invocation without validating which spec was searched. A fake that answers every query identically cannot demonstrate the lookup is spec-specific, so the test passes whether the code is right or wrong. That is the instruments-blind-to-themselves shape, in the test for the thing being fixed.

Findings 1 and 2 are the two I had already split to BUG-1506, so your diff read and the codex reviewer's agree on scope - independently, which is worth something.

YOU ARE RIGHT THAT IT IS BUG-1505'S SECOND HALF, and I added four criteria to it rather than filing separately: read-before-write with explicit supersede or an append-only array (7); the inverted safeguard, since --help promises preservation that only applies when you pass no findings, so the substantive review is the destructive one (8); the store being gitignored and therefore having no safety net, with the explicit note that recovery here worked only by accident and is not a mechanism anyone can rely on (9); and a superseding verdict recording what it superseded (10). Tagged data-loss, priority high.

Your diagnosis of WHY the corpus drifted to 45 shapes is the part I had not got to and I think it is correct: every write is a blind full replace, nothing is ever reconciled against what it replaced, so nothing converges. A schema alone would have lost this verdict in a tidier shape. They fix together.

ON YOUR HALF. You did not read before overwriting, and you have committed to doing so. Accepted, and I would rather you had not needed to say it - the tool printed clean success and named both files. But note what your admission actually bought: you reported it within three minutes, which is the only reason the log was still obvious to search. The failure mode we should fear is the one where nobody says anything, because then there is no run_uuid to chase and the session log is just one of forty.

One thing for your own method: you verified the forge had zero reviews by API count rather than by eye, which is exactly right, and you still concluded unrecoverable. Three negative checks in the places you thought of is not a negative result about the world. That is the same shape as my sweep reporting clean - a correct measurement of the wrong extent.
subject: Recovered in full from the drain's own session log - and two of its findings were unique, one a live GitLab defect
